evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: "I'll just have a few questions to give you the most accurate code. This would take ten to fifteen minutes and then before I proceed aside from the pricing, do you have any other concerns about the moving process?" — time-boxed but no explicit promise of a dependable quote, and no clear wait for a yes before moving to details.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked as "aside from the pricing, do you have any other concerns about the moving process?" — but this came after already gathering name, phone, email, and pickup address. Should have been asked before any probing started.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer answered "No, thank you" to concerns question. N/A — no concerns raised to follow up on.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection of concerns back to customer (though N/A since no concerns were raised).
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (apartment), floor (third floor, no elevator at origin; first floor at destination), rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (close to stairs, less than six feet to apartment), box count (15–25 boxes), special considerations (no workout equipment, no piano, no valuables, no large appliances). All seven items addressed.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: "normally ma'am, if we're only moving a one bedroom apartment worth of items we see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?" — yes, asked.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. No version of "Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?" appears in the transcript.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "I estimate the move to finish in three hours to four hours with two movers and one truck. So, the estimated cost for this move is $7.74298 million" — hourly rate ($104/mover, $208 total), travel fee ($150), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments all disclosed. Personalized to third-floor, stair-access scenario. Anchor is present and personalized.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full transparency: $104/hr per mover ($208 total), $150 travel fee, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, all included (gas, truck, insurance, pads, tools). "No hidden fees of any type." Present and clear.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: After estimate, rep says "Would you like to be on the schedule? No deposit is required." — never asks "Does that feel fair?" and no pause offered for customer reaction. Rep moves directly to booking ask.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: No mention of On-Time Guarantee or any discount terms for lateness.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: No mention of No Worries Damage Coverage, $2,000 coverage, or built-in damage protection.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No version of "Does that put those to rest?" asked. No section closing.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asks "What's still concerning you about this move?" or any genuine final concerns check. No final check at all.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No version of "Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?" appears.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: "Would you like to be on the schedule? No deposit is required." — asked, but immediately softened with "No deposit is required," which functions as an implicit out and reduces urgency.

top_strength: Jeline gathered all seven logistics details efficiently (property type, floors, walking distances, box count, special items) and disclosed pricing and fees with transparency and clarity before the customer could ask.
coaching_note: Skip the Two Promises section entirely — On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage were never mentioned; these are load-bearing trust-builders and must be delivered before the ask, not omitted. Additionally, after giving the estimate, ask "Does that feel fair?" and hold genuine silence rather than pivoting immediately to "Would you like to be on the schedule?"
